context.problemStatement:
Implement the `Lambda` case of `eval`. An anonymous function `fn(x) { ... }`
evaluates to a function value. Nothing in its body is evaluated until it is
called, so this case never returns an error. Build a `VFunc(UserFn(...))` whose
name is `"lambda"` (used in error messages) and whose parent is the environment
in which this function was *defined*, not the one in which it will be called. This
is what lets a function use the names around it, even after the call that created it
has returned.

```
// In eval:
    Lambda(params, body) ->
      // YOUR CODE HERE (replace the code below)
      Error(errors.NotImplemented(
        "Lambda("
        <> string.inspect(params)
        <> ", "
        <> string.inspect(body)
        <> ")",
      ))
```

Run the tests:

```
gleam test -- q8
```

targets.claim: Student can explain why their Lambda case never returns an error even when the body of the anonymous function uses an unbound name, and when such an error would appear instead.

probes.question: If `body` in `Lambda(params, body)` contains an unbound variable name, why does evaluating this `Lambda` case still succeed with `Ok`, and when would an error actually be raised?
probes.reason: Directly asks the student to explain why constructing the lambda value ignores errors in the body and precisely when those errors will surface.

probes.question: In your `Lambda(params, body)` branch, what happens to `body` during `eval`, and at what point in program execution would any expressions inside it be evaluated?
probes.reason: Provides an alternate angle focusing on how `body` is handled in the AST evaluation step versus invocation.

content: If `body` in `Lambda(params, body)` contains an unbound variable name, why does evaluating this `Lambda` case still succeed with `Ok`, and when would an error actually be raised?
Lambda constructs a function value without evaluating its body. The error only occurs when the lambda is called

reason: The student correctly explained both parts of the claim: evaluating a lambda merely constructs the function value without evaluating the body, and the unbound name error would only occur when the function is actually called.
